title: Which angles does a slanting fold make in a sheet?
description: A rectangular sheet is folded along a slanting crease EF, and the four angles between the crease and the long sides are named. One angle is traced and laid over the others with the vertices together, and the same check is run on a second pair. The largest and smallest angles are read from where the second arm falls.
teaching_notes: One idea: name each angle with its vertex as the middle letter, then compare by tracing and laying one over another. Watch for students who count only two angles, one at each end of the crease.

video_script.why: The child names the angles made by a crease and compares them by tracing and laying one over another.
video_script.substitution: a rectangular sheet ABCD with a slanting crease EF from the side AB to the side DC
video_script.anchor: a rectangular sheet of paper with a slanting crease
video_script.payoff_line: Angle eigh ee eff and angle see eff ee are the larger angles

final_answer.value: angle AEF and angle CFE are larger than angle BEF and angle DFE
final_answer.spoken: angle eigh ee eff and angle see eff ee are the larger angles, and angle bee ee eff and angle dee eff ee are the smaller angles

maths_rules: the sheet is the rectangle ABCD, with the long sides AB and DC
the crease EF runs from E on AB to F on DC, slanting to the right as it goes down
four angles are formed: AEF and BEF at E, DFE and CFE at F, each with the vertex as the middle letter
AEF and CFE are larger than BEF and DFE (the worklist's example of the book)
compare by tracing one angle and laying it on another with the vertices together and one arm along one arm
check: trace BEF and lay it on CFE, and its second arm falls inside, so BEF is smaller
with another fold the largest and smallest angles change
video_script.design: One idea: name the four angles and compare them by superimposition, the way the book compares angles. One rectangle with one crease stays on the board.
open_questions: Which angles are larger comes from the worklist's example of the book; the book's figure could not be viewed.
